Subject: POC: Success criteria, timelines & initial risk tracker

Hi Alex —

Great to meet you today. Per our discovery call, I wanted to capture the POC plan, proposed success criteria, owners, and an initial risk tracker so we have clear expectations. Attaching two files: poc_success_criteria.xlsx (one-pager) and poc_risk_tracker.csv (live tracker).

POC summary (2-week trial):
- Goal: Validate Redwood's hosted inference for product search ranking (latency & relevance).
- Scope: ~10k queries/day, 2 concurrent product ingestion pipelines, sample data subset (anonymized).

Success criteria (proposed):
1) Relevance: NDCG@10 improvement >= 5% vs baseline on your eval set.
2) Latency: 95th percentile inference latency < 150ms for 512-token requests.
3) Stability: <1% error rate during the trial window.
4) Integration: Data connector and test harness ingest working end-to-end by day 3.

Evaluation plan & timeline:
- Day 0-2: Access & data handoff (Stellar provides anonymized sample + credentials). Owner: Alex
- Day 2-4: Ingest + baseline runs. Owner: Dev (Redwood)
- Day 5-10: Evaluation runs + metric reports. Owner: Marissa/Rishi
- Day 11-14: Decision & next steps (expand to full dataset or plan for production).

Risks & mitigations (see tracker):
- Data access delays -> mitigation: temporary sample upload to our secure S3 (Dev to coordinate).
- Query schema mismatch -> mitigation: small mapping adapter (1-2 days).
- Blocking inference bug -> mitigation: priority escalation to Rishi, open SUP ticket; we will provide a rollback/workaround plan.

Next steps:
1) Alex: confirm sample dataset availability and any security contacts by EOD Monday.
2) Dev: provision sandbox for Stellar and share credentials.
3) Rishi/Marissa: schedule daily 15-min standups for first 5 days.

Thanks — let me know if you want to tweak the success criteria.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and aligns with our internal expectations. A few clarifications:

- Data: We can provide an anonymized sample tonight (csv + mapping). I will loop in our security team (security@stellarcommerce.com) for the access approval.
- Latency: 150ms P95 sounds achievable; if you can show 200ms we'd still be in an acceptable band for the team.
- Integration: We have a pipeline that produces JSONL; will that be fine for ingestion?

Blockers to flag now:
1) Our security/compliance team requires an inventory of where the data will be stored and whether Redwood will persist tokens beyond the trial. They asked for a SOC2 evidence pointer.
2) If we need to run larger runs in the middle of the trial, we may need a short increase in quota.

Action: I can send the sample tonight and introduce you to our security lead. Can you confirm who will own the security Q&A on your side?
